cloud_identity.title: The Global Namespace Risk: Universal Bucket Hijacking Technique for Cloud Data Exfiltration
cloud_identity.notes: Threat Research (author Yahav Festinger). After compromising a cloud environment and obtaining delete permissions, an attacker can delete a target storage bucket and immediately recreate one with the same name in their own account, redirecting the victim's data stream — abusing global bucket-name uniqueness across major CSPs. New cloud-exfil TTP angle (bucket hijacking / namespace squatting); mitigations: least-privilege on delete actions, AWS data-perimeter SCP / VPC-endpoint policies. No tracked actor; maps loosely to T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage Object), T1537 (Transfer Data to Cloud Account), T1074 (Data Staged). P1 — did NOT meet weekly-canvas draft-stub gate (not a P0 actor profile / anatomy / IR / active-exploitation advisory).

cloud_identity.title: Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility
cloud_identity.notes: GAP-WINDOW CATCH (published 2026-06-09, outside the 2026-06-22..2026-06-29 canvas window; surfaced during the Unit 42 homepage sweep and was missed by prior weekly canvases). Threat Research on attackers abusing cloud logging services (e.g., disabling/tampering CloudTrail and equivalent CSP logs) to evade detection and blind defenders. Distinct from the already-indexed defensive piece 'Novel Technique to Detect Cloud Threat Actor Operations' (tracking-threat-groups-through-cloud-logging) — this is the OFFENSIVE inverse. No tracked actor; maps to T1562 (Impair Defenses), specifically T1562.008 (Disable or Modify Cloud Logs), plus T1578 (Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure). P1 index-only: T1562.008 would be NEW MITRE technique coverage for the corpus, so it does NOT qualify for an autonomous draft stub. OPERATOR REVIEW: (1) decide whether to author a cloud-defense-evasion TTP; (2) if so, T1562.008 is a new technique enum to add to corpus MITRE coverage.

Corroborates the existing SRC-NCSC-UK edge-device cross-reference (Fortinet/VPN gateway targeting). Detection/IR data source for data staging (T1074), archive-collected (T1560), and indicator removal / anti-forensics (T1070). Parse with ccl-segb. No new actor/TTP -> P1 reference for macOS data-exfil detection. New 'detection_engineering' group created for detection-relevant research.

credential_attacks.title: Threat Brief: Mitigating Large-Scale Credential Attacks ("FortiBleed")
credential_attacks.notes: High Profile Threats threat brief on a large-scale password-spraying + credential-theft campaign ('FortiBleed') against internet-exposed Fortinet, Sophos, and MSSQL services; multi-stage (spray -> config/credential extraction via priv-esc -> offline cracking -> persistent admin access). An initial access broker on Russian-language forum Exploit[.]in claimed the campaign and began selling harvested credentials on 2026-06-16, referencing an unspecified CVE. Not targeting PANW devices; Unit 42 published out of an abundance of caution with hardening/MFA/ZTNA guidance. Maps to T1110 / T1110.003 (Brute Force / Password Spraying), T1078 (Valid Accounts), T1003 (credential extraction from device config). P0 active-exploitation advisory, but does NOT meet weekly-canvas draft-stub gate: the threat actor is an unnamed IAB not in scope_seeds.actors. OPERATOR REVIEW: (1) decide whether to add an actor/cluster label once Unit 42 names it; (2) confirm whether T1110 password-spraying warrants new MITRE technique coverage in the corpus.
